affectedPublicSurfaces: NO SELLER-VISIBLE SURFACE IN THIS SLICE, by design. It is one additive migration plus the model classes that must match it. Nothing reads the new columns; P-SHARED-2 (#1702) is the first reader. The acceptance criteria are deliberately schema-level for exactly that reason.

The surface it DOES have is every existing /v1 route and worker that touches `workflow_runs` or `action_cards` while the migration is in force. `product_id` becomes nullable and two unique constraints are re-keyed, so the honest verification is that today's behaviour is unchanged: an authenticated decisions read, a run listing, and the card refresh path all continue to work against the migrated schema with the OLD code still running.

migrationCompatibility.notes: Migration number 061 is RESERVED BY META for this issue - do not compute down_revision from head. 059 and 060 are already on main (#1966, #1968) and no other in-flight branch adds a migration. Expand only: columns are added with defaults, product_id widens from NOT NULL to nullable, and the new uniques are created before the old action_cards unique is dropped in the same migration. Old code keeps running because every new column has a default and no old query names a dropped column. The one contraction is the old (shop_id, workflow_key) unique on action_cards, which is a constraint drop, not a data drop.

rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: alembic downgrade -1 restores the old constraints; it MUST fail loudly rather than silently discard if any row carries a non-product subject or a NULL product_id, because those rows cannot be represented under the old NOT NULL constraint

doNotInfer: MIGRATION NUMBER 061 IS RESERVED BY META. Use it. Never read the next number from head and never compute down_revision dynamically - other waves are open and that is how two migrations collide on one revision.

DO NOT ADD A READER. Nothing in this slice may query, filter or branch on workflow_key, subject_type, subject_ref, subject_id, revision or supersedes_card_id. #1702 is the first reader. A reader here would make the slice unreviewable against 'nothing behavioural changes'.
ADR-087's status stays Proposed. It flips to Accepted in P-SHARED-3's PR, not this one.

THE SQLITE TRAP: the `session` fixture in this suite is SQLite even when DATABASE_URL is set, and SQLite silently tolerates constraint semantics Postgres rejects. A partial unique index and a NOT NULL widening are exactly the claims SQLite cannot falsify. Every constraint assertion in these tests must run against real Postgres - use the disposable-database pattern in tests/integration/test_agent_runner_concurrency.py::_disposable_postgres_url, and say plainly in the artifact which assertions ran on which engine.

THE ROUND TRIP IS upgrade -> downgrade -> upgrade, not upgrade alone, and the backfill must be asserted on rows that EXISTED BEFORE the upgrade - seed them first, then migrate. A backfill tested only against rows created after the migration proves nothing.

A guard must be seen failing (.cursor/rules/code-quality.mdc): for each new constraint test, make it go red on purpose - drop the partial unique, or insert the colliding row - print what came back, and report both states.
Pin PYTHONPATH="$PWD/backend/src:$PWD" for any pytest run inside the worktree, or the green is fake.

Follow the exemplars named in CLAUDE.md's code-standard table rather than inventing a second shape: backend/src/juli_backend/repositories/_base.py and commerce.py for repositories, tests/unit/test_repositories_base.py for tests.
Writes stay sandbox-bound. Never touch Fujiwa Vietnam Store (2b1da87b-d0a8-46a6-b3c6-2132be0b5f4f) and never run a migration against production.
